text.p: China's stock markets rebounded strongly at noon on Thursday after an initial steep fall on news of the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, and analysts said they were surprised by the strength and speed of the return.
Both Shanghai and Shenzhen's B share indices were up slightly after dropping almost limit-down 10 percent in the first few minutes after the markets opened.
The Shanghai B index was up 0.29 percent or 0.188 points at 65.318, while Shenzhen was up 0.63 percent or 0.89 points at 142.64.

Alex Conroy, an analyst with ING-Barings in Shanghai said the sequence of a fall followed by a rebound in the aftermath of Deng's death had long been expected, but the speed of the reaction was surprising.
"It's happening a bit faster than I expected," she said.
Brokers said prices were supported by widespread bargain hunting and heavy support by institutions.

"Institutional support was very strong which boosted the confidence of investors," said a local broker. "Also, the rumours about Deng a couple of days ago limited the impact today quite considerably."
Brokers said they expected the markets to maintain their current levels during afternoon trading, but many did not rule out the possibility of further falls in the coming days.

"The Deng news attracted a huge amount of bargain-hunting from investors aiming for quick profits," said a Shanghai broker. "But the market will soon enter a period of correction after the recent unheavals."
In Shenzhen, brokers said they still expected the market to trend lower in the near future despite the strong rebound, with trading seen by some as turning increasingly volatile in the near future.
"I expect stocks to close lower for the next two days," said one broker in Shenzhen.
At noon, the Shanghai A share index was down 2.49 percent or 25.018 points at 979.932 while the Shenzhen A index was down 3.78 percent or 13.52 points at 344.61.
